title: Logframe simulation playground — compatibility checklist & rollback scenarios (v0.1)
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a lightweight simulation playground for validating audit-log schema changes across v1→v2→v3, a compatibility checklist we can run before rolling changes, and concrete rollback scenarios for SIEM export and evidence automation. The aim is pragmatic: give SRE/Security/Platform a repeatable set of tests to signal safe deploy versus abort.

Background/Context (short):
- We have three active schema cohorts in the wild (internal v1 traces, mid-stage v2 with RBAC enrichments, and experimental v3 with evidence linking).
- Customers and SIEM partners expect stable field names and idempotent event identity.
- Recent CI runs uncovered gaps around: partial enrichment, null vs missing fields, and a new evidence.link array shape.

Scope of this doc:
- Define simulation scenarios (how to synthesize traffic representing multiple schema versions).
- Provide a compatibility checklist (binary checks + soft recommendations).
- List rollback decision points and practical mitigations for SIEM ingestion.
- Provide small example frames and jq/snippets teams can run locally.

Quick definitions:
- FRAME: single audit event flattened for ship; a logline with key/value fields we assert on.
- COHORT: set of producers emitting a particular shape (v1, v2, v3).
- EVIDENCE LINKING: ability to attach evidence ids and blobs to an event payload (v3 experiment).

Simulation scenarios (minimal set to run pre-rollout):
1) Basic parity: 1000 v1 frames -> transform pass-through to v2 shape. Verify field presence and no dropped identifiers.
2) Enrichment failure: simulate partial enrich (Auth user resolved intermittently). Confirm downstream shows both enriched and fallback fields.
3) Evidence attach: simulate v3 frames with evidence.link array; check SIEM exporter converts to single-string fingerprint column without truncation.
4) Mixed-cohort burst: simulate concurrent v1/v2/v3 bursts to validate router and transform pipeline preserves provenance headers.
5) Redaction path: simulate reasoned PII redaction (masking) and verify retained audit id for correlation.

Sample frames (flat text examples to paste into tests):
- v1 example frame (legacy minimal):
  producer=auth-service event_type=login user_id=U-12345 timestamp=2026-02-14T22:11:09Z request_id=RID-0ab4 status=success

- v2 example frame (RBAC enrichments):
  producer=auth-service event_type=login user_id=U-12345 user_role=svc:app-backend role_id=R-77 timestamp=2026-02-14T22:11:09Z request_id=RID-0ab4 status=success auth_method=oauth2

- v3 example frame (evidence linking + nested-fingerprint flattened):
  producer=auth-service event_type=login user_id=U-12345 user_role=svc:app-backend role_id=R-77 timestamp=2026-02-14T22:11:09Z request_id=RID-0ab4 status=success evidence_link_ids=EID-9a2c;EID-19b3 evidence_fingerprint=sha256:3f2c...

Compatibility checklist (automatable checks we should run end-to-end):
- Identity stability: request_id and user_id must be present or a documented mapping must exist for the cohort. (hard fail)
- Field type stability: same field names must not flip types (string→object). If type change is unavoidable, add new field with clear deprecation TTL. (hard fail)
- Null vs missing: standardize on absent field (missing) rather than field: null for all newly-introduced optional fields. (soft fail if mismatch)
- Evidence fields: arrays must serialize to a single deterministic delimited string for SIEM X (legacy column). If we cannot, add a canonical fingerprint field. (hard fail for SIEM export)
- RBAC enrichment: role_id must be idempotent across retries; if enrichment service fails, add role_source=unresolved. (warning)
- Timestamp canonicalization: all frames must include an iso8601 timestamp in UTC and an ingestion_time set by the shipper. (hard fail)

Export mapping guide (SIEM column recommendations):
- siem_req_id => request_id
- siem_actor => user_id || anonymous
- siem_role => role_id (if present)
- siem_evidence => evidence_fingerprint (if evidence_link_ids present fallback to join(evidence_link_ids, ';'))
- siem_event => event_type
- siem_ts => timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)

Rollback decision tree (practical):
- If >2% of frames in canary have missing request_id OR change in type: abort and rollback transform.
- If SIEM consumers report parse errors for >1 hour after canary: automatically revert exporter to compatibility mode (exporter has v1-compat toggle).
- If evidence_fingerprint collisions detected in sampling: disable evidence_fingerprint column and continue exporting raw evidence_link_ids as delimited list while we investigate.

Example jq checks for local simulation (run against newline-delimited frames):
- check missing request_id: jq -R 'fromjson? // {} | select(.request_id==null) | .event_type' (returns offending events)
- normalize evidence array to fingerprint placeholder: jq -r 'fromjson? | .evidence_link_ids // [] | join(";")'
- assert timestamp ISO: jq -r 'fromjson? | .timestamp | test("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}T")'

Testing matrix (minimal):
- Unit: schema linter (CI) for new fields and deprecations.
- Integration: simulated exporter -> collector -> SIEM parser in staging.
- Load: mixed-cohort burst at 5x peak for 10 minutes. Verify no field loss.
- Privacy: redaction tests for PII fields (sample set and heuristics).

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Do we prefer adding 'evidence_fingerprint' as a stable column for SIEM compatibility or convert SIEM to accept evidence_link_ids as multi-values? Immediate stopgap: add fingerprint column (less change to SIEM).
- How long do we maintain v1 compatibility headers? Recommend 90 days after last external consumer sign-off.
- What is acceptable tolerance for enrichment misses during peak? Recommend 1% for first 7 days of rollout, then tighten.

Next steps / runbook (short):
1) Create small staging job to synthesize 10k mixed frames (v1/v2/v3) and run through exporter.
2) Run the checklist above and capture summary report (automated).
3) If all green, run 1-hour canary at 10% traffic with exporter v2 compat toggles on.
4) Monitor SIEM ingestion errors and request_id preservation; abort on hard-fail signals.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call rollback message (copy/paste):
- "Rolling back logframe schema transform to previous hash (deploy #) due to compatibility errors. Exporter toggled to v1-compat. Investigating enrichment failures and evidence mapping. Contact: @Maya, #sec-telemetry"

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a pragmatic playground doc to help teams simulate and triage. Please add simulation scripts or small sample payloads you want included.
- If you own an exporter or SIEM integration, please add your parsing quirks to linked_artifacts so we can expand the mapping table.

End of doc.
